Rashi on Chullin 29a:11:1.english: It needs the blood - For the sprinkling [of the blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 29a:15:1.hebrew: מליקתו כשרה מיבעי ליה - כלומר, אעוף איבעי ליה למיתני מליקתו כשרה, והדר ליתני אבהמה שחיטתה כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:15:1.english: "Its pinching [melikah] is valid" he should have said - That is to say, with regard to a bird, he should have taught "its pinching is valid," and then taught with regard to an animal, "its slaughter is valid."

Rashi on Chullin 29a:15:2.hebrew: הא לא קשיא - גבי הדדי תננהו, וכי סליק מבהמה נקט שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:15:2.english: This is not difficult - [The mishna] taught them [both, the slaughter and the pinching] next to each other, and when it finished [discussing] animals, it took up slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:15:3.english: Rather, the first clause - Where [the mishna] taught, "One who slaughters."

Rashi on Chullin 29a:15:4.hebrew: מכדי בעוף קאי - ובו התחיל להורות, והיכי סמך ליה שחיטה בעוף קדשים? המולק מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:15:4.english: Since [the mishna] is dealing with a bird - And with it [the bird] it began to teach. And how can it juxtapose to it slaughter in a bird of sacrifices? It should have said "one who nips [the neck]"!

Rashi on Chullin 29a:17:1.hebrew: ה"ג: מאי רוב אחד? רוב כל אחד ואחד, ולא גרסינן "אלא":
Rashi on Chullin 29a:17:1.english: This is the correct text: "What is 'a majority of one'? A majority of each and every one [of the two signs]." And we do not have the text "But..." [here].

Rashi on Chullin 29a:17:2.hebrew: לא פסיקא ליה - ותנא מילתא דמישתמע בתרוייהו דהכי משמע: רוב כל אחד בעוף כשרה. היכא דסגי בחד, כגון חטאת, הוי רובו ככולו, והיכא דבעי תרתי, הוי רוב כל אחד ככולו:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:17:2.english: It was not clear to him - And the Tanna [stated] a matter that can be understood in both ways, for this is what it means: [If one cut] the majority of each one [of the two pipes] in a bird, it is valid. Where one is sufficient, such as a sin-offering, the majority of it is considered like all of it; and where two are required, the majority of each one is considered like all of it.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:18:1.hebrew: שפיר - מש"ה פליגי רבנן עליה, דכיון דלא הוזכרו וורידין אלא משום דם, מה לי בשעת שחיטה ומה לי לאחר שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:18:1.english: It is fine - For this reason the Rabbis disagree with him, since the veins are mentioned only because of the blood: what difference does it make whether it is at the time of slaughter or after slaughter?

Rashi on Chullin 29a:18:2.hebrew: אלא בקדשים - היכי פליגי רבנן עליה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:18:2.english: Rather, [it is] with sacrificial animals - How do the Rabbis disagree with him?

Rashi on Chullin 29a:18:3.hebrew: הוא עצמו - כל עצמה ועיקרה של שחיטת קדשים לדם היא צריכה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:18:3.english: Itself - The entire essence and main purpose of the slaughter of sacrificial animals is needed for the blood.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:1:1.hebrew: כדי שחיטה אחרת - היינו שיעור שהייה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:1:1.english: Enough time for another slaughter - That is, the measure of a delay [that disqualifies the slaughter].

Rashi on Chullin 29a:1:2.hebrew: וגמרה - קס"ד בבהמה קאי, דבעיא רוב שנים, ומאי "גמרה"? לשחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:1:2.english: And he completed it - It enters one's mind [to say] that this refers to an animal, which requires the majority of two [organs]; and what is "he completed it"? He completed the slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:1:3.hebrew: ואי מחצה כרוב - כיון דשהה בחצי, אזלא לה שחיטה, והויא לה כפגימה בעלמא, ואיטרפא לה בפסוקת הגרגרת. אלא ש"מ אינו כרוב, ופסוקת הגרגרת ברובא בעינן:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:1:3.english: And if half is like a majority - Since he paused at the half, the slaughter is gone, and it is [treated] as a mere notch, and [the animal] becomes a *tereifa* through a severed windpipe. But [since it is not a *tereifa*,] learn from this that [half] is not like a majority, and [for] a severed windpipe we require a majority:

Rashi on Chullin 29a:20:1.hebrew: תזבח - לרצונכם תזבחוהו. ואמרינן לקמן: "תזבחהו" כתיב, ויש אם למסורת. "תזבח" משמע דלשוחט יחידי קאמר, ולא לשנים, מדלא כתיב "תזבחוהו". ומדכתיב "הוא" משמע נמי "אזבח", שאף הוא יהא יחידי:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:20:1.english: You shall slaughter - You shall slaughter it of your own will. And we say later [that the word] "tizbaḥehu" is written [without a vav], and "there is a basis for the traditional reading." "Tizbaḥ" implies that [Scripture] speaks of a single slaughterer and not two, since it did not write "tizbeḥuhu" [in the plural]. And since it wrote "hu" (it), this also implies "I shall slaughter," meaning that he too must be alone.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:21:1.hebrew: ואמר רב כהנא - גרסינן. הא דר"ל בסדר יומא (דף לב:) גבי הביאו לו לכ"ג את התמיד:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:21:1.english: And Rav Kahana said - This is the reading we have. This [statement] of Reish Lakish is in the order of Yoma (page 32b), regarding [the mishna:] They brought the daily offering to the High Priest.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:23:1.hebrew: קרצו - מפרשינן התם: ברוב שנים, שלא היה יכול למרק ולגמור את השחיטה כולה, לפי שכל עבודת יה"כ אינה כשרה אלא בו, דכתיב באחרי מות וכפר הכהן אשר ימשח אותו, והיה צריך לאחוז מהר את המזרק ולקבל הדם. לפיכך חותך בו כדי הכשר שחיטה ומניחה, וממהר לקבל:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:23:1.english: He nicked it - We explain there [that this refers to cutting] the majority of two [signs], because he could not polish and finish the entire slaughter, since all the service of Yom Kippur is valid only when performed by him, as it is written in Acharei Mot, "And the priest who is anointed shall atone"; and he needed to quickly take hold of the basin and receive the blood. Therefore he cuts in it (the animal) enough for a valid slaughter, and leaves it, and hurries to receive [the blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 29a:23:2.english: And he completed [the slaughter] - Another priest, after the slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:23:3.hebrew: על ידו - בשבילו, כמו (עירובין דף פב:) "מערב אדם על יד בנו ובתו", בשבילם. ומפני ששנינו שם דצריך למרק, יכול לא מירק יהא פסול, דבקדשים לא סגי ברוב שנים:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:23:3.english: By his hand - On his behalf, like [the phrase] (Eiruvin 82b) "a person may establish an eiruv by the hand of his son and daughter," meaning on their behalf. And because we learned there [in the mishna] that he needs to complete the slaughter, one might think that if he did not complete it, it would be invalid, since with sacrificial offerings, a majority of two [sim. the majority of both organs] is not sufficient.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:2:1.hebrew: לא בעוף - דממה נפשך כשרה, כדמפרש:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:2:1.english: Not in a bird - For either way [the bird] is valid, as [the Gemara] explains.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:2:2.hebrew: הא עבד ליה רובא - ואיתכשרא מקמי שהייה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:2:2.english: But he has already performed the majority - And it became valid before the delay.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:2:3.hebrew: לא עבד ליה כלום - מעשה טרפה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:2:3.english: It did not accomplish anything for it - The act [of causing] a treifa.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:3:1.english: Half of the windpipe damaged - In a bird.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:4:1.hebrew: רוב הנראה לעינים - כלומר, רוב גמור שהוא ניכר:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:4:1.english: A majority that is visible to the eyes - That is, a complete majority that is noticeable.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:5:1.hebrew: מה טרפה - דאיכא מקומות טובא דמיטרפא בהו במשהו, כגון נקובת הוושט והריאה והדקין:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:5:1.english: Just as with a tereifa - For there are many places where [an animal] becomes a tereifa through the slightest [defect], such as a perforation of the gullet, the lung, and the small intestines.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:5:2.hebrew: בעינן רוב הנראה לעינים - במקומות שהוזכר בהן רוב, כגון בקנה ובחוט השדרה:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:5:2.english: We require the majority that is visible to the eyes - In the places where a majority is mentioned, such as in the windpipe and in the spinal cord.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:5:3.hebrew: שחיטה דעד דאיכא רובא לא מתכשרא - דאפילו מאן דמכשר, משום דקרי ליה רובא הוא, ובמיעוטא כולהו מודו:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:5:3.english: Slaughter up to the point where there is a majority does not render it valid - For even the one who deems it valid [in the case of half and half] does so because it is called a majority; but in the case of a minority, all agree [that it is not valid].

Rashi on Chullin 29a:7:1.hebrew: מחצה על מחצה כרוב - וטהורים עושין לעצמן בטהרה, וטמאין עושין לעצמן בטומאה, ולא מידחו לפסח שני כיחידין:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:7:1.english: Half against half is like a majority - And the pure ones perform [the Paschal offering] for themselves in a state of purity, and the impure ones perform it for themselves in a state of impurity, and they are not deferred to the Second Pesach like individuals.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:7:2.english: It is not a majority - And the impure ones are set aside for the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Chullin 29a:8:1.hebrew: והתם מאי טעמא דרב - הא בעלמא אמרת דלא הוי רובא:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:8:1.english: And there, what is Rav's reason? - For elsewhere you say that it is not a majority.

Rashi on Chullin 29a:8:2.hebrew: דכתיב איש איש כי יהיה טמא - ידחה לשני, ופלגא נהי דרובא לא מיקרי, מיהו מכלל יחידין נפקי להו ולא מידחו:
Rashi on Chullin 29a:8:2.english: For it is written, "Any man [ish ish] who is impure" - [The verse implies that] he is to be pushed off to the second [Passover]. And [regarding] half: granted that it is not called a majority, nevertheless they have left the category of individuals, and so they are not pushed off.

Tosafot on Chullin 29a:12:1.hebrew: אבל בחולין דלאו לדם הוא צריך אימא בפלגא סגי - והא דקתני חצי אחד בעוף ואחד וחצי בבהמה שחיטתה פסולה, היינו סיפא דאיירי בקדשים:
Tosafot on Chullin 29a:12:1.english: But with regard to unconsecrated animals (ḥullin), where it is not needed for the blood, one might say that half suffices - And as for that which [the Mishnah] teaches that [if only] one half in a bird, or one and a half [organs] in an animal, [was cut], its slaughter is invalid, that is the latter clause, which deals with consecrated animals (kodashim):

Tosafot on Chullin 29a:23:1.hebrew: ומירק אחר שחיטתו על ידו - מירק, לשון גמר, כדאמרינן במדרש: מי שהתחיל במצוה, אומרים לו מרוק:
Tosafot on Chullin 29a:23:1.english: And he [the Kohen] performed *mirek* after its slaughter, by his own hand - *Mirek* is an expression of finishing, as we say in the Midrash: One who began a mitzvah, they say to him, "Finish (*maruk*) it."

Tosafot on Chullin 29a:6:1.hebrew: דכולי עלמא מחצה על מחצה אינו כרוב - וא"ת, דבפ"ק דעירובין (דף טז: ושם) פסקינן כרב פפא דאמר פרוץ כעומד מותר, והיה נראה לחלק בין שאר איסורין בדבר התלוי בחיות, אי לאו דמייתי עלה לעיל דתנור. וגם תימה, דבעירובין לא מייתי לה, והנהו דמייתי התם לא מייתי הכא. ושמא יש לחלק, דהכא איסור וטומאה, והתם לענין מחיצות, ולא דמי:
Tosafot on Chullin 29a:6:1.english: Everyone agrees that half and half is not [considered] a majority - And if you ask: In the first chapter of Eruvin (16b, and there), we rule like Rav Pappa, who said that a breach [comprising the majority] is treated like something standing, [and so] it is permitted. And it would have appeared [reasonable] to distinguish between other prohibitions and a matter dependent on life, were it not that [the Gemara] cited a proof for it earlier, regarding the oven. And it is also astonishing, for in Eruvin it does not cite this [principle], and those [sources] that it cites there it does not cite here. But perhaps one can distinguish, [saying] that here [we deal with] prohibition and impurity, while there [it concerns] the laws of partitions, and they are not comparable:

Tosafot on Chullin 29a:8:1.hebrew: איש נדחה ואין ציבור נדחין - תימה, דבפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף טז.) גבי "והוצאת את האיש ההוא" וגו', דרשינן: איש ואשה אתה מוציא לשעריך, ואי אתה מוציא כל השבט כולו לשעריך; והכא לא ממעטי מאיש אלא רוב ישראל? וי"ל, דהתם מצינו שחילק הכתוב בין יחיד למרובים משום עיר בעלמא לענין עיר הנדחת, לפיכך מסתברא לחלק משום שבט, ולומר דלא מיקרי איש. א"נ, טובא איש ואשה כתיבי התם:
Tosafot on Chullin 29a:8:1.english: An individual may be deferred, but the community may not be deferred - It is puzzling: for in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (16a), regarding "and you shall bring out that man" etc., we derive: you may bring out a man or a woman to your gates, but you may not bring out an entire tribe to your gates. And here, do we exclude only the majority of Israel from [the term] "man" (ish)? And one may answer: there, we find that the verse distinguished between an individual and many [people] on account of a mere city, with regard to the condemned city (ir hanidachat); therefore it is reasonable to distinguish on account of a tribe as well, and to say that [a tribe] is not called "a man." Alternatively, [the words] "man" and "woman" are written many times there.
